key_insight: Machine learning can accurately predict and help optimize the tensile strength and micro-hardness of AA6082–AA7075 friction stir welded joints from a small set of welding parameters.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that data-driven models can guide parameter selection in friction stir welding to improve joint performance and reduce trial-and-error experimentation.
method: Inputs: tool rotational speed, traverse speed, and plunge depth.
Outputs: ultimate tensile strength and micro-hardness.
Compared five regressors: LR, RF, SVR, XGBoost, and KNN with an 80:20 train-test split.
evidence_signal: Random Forest gave the best UTS prediction on the test set (MAE 9.007 MPa, RMSE 12.975 MPa), while SVR with an RBF kernel was best for micro-hardness (MAE 0.923 HV, RMSE 1.155 HV).
watch_item: Performance is based on a limited experimental dataset, so generalization to other materials, tool geometries, or welding setups should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Explainable machine learning approach for predicting mechanical characteristics of AA6082–AA7075 friction stir welded joints
